core.headline: End-of-terrace Victorian cottage in Smarden Conservation Area
core.listing:
This end-of-terrace Victorian cottage stands in red brick under a clay-tiled roof in Smarden Conservation Area. Built around 1880, number 2 Forge Cottages offers two-bedroom accommodation on The Street, with on-street parking.

The sitting room measures 3.90m x 3.60m (12'10" x 11'10") and has a cast-iron fireplace. The kitchen/dining room measures 4.30m x 3.20m (14'1" x 10'6") and has a quarry-tiled floor, a range alcove and reclaimed beams dating from the 1990s. Ledged-and-braced doors are fitted throughout. The bathroom is on the first floor.

Bedroom 1 measures 3.80m x 3.30m (12'6" x 10'10"). Bedroom 2 measures 2.90m x 2.40m (9'6" x 7'10").

The rear cottage garden extends approximately 12m (40ft), with a brick path and timber shed.

The village pub is approximately 2 minutes' walk.

Guide Price £425,000 for the freehold. Council Tax band C (Ashford Borough Council). EPC rating E. Construction: standard – red brick under a clay-tiled roof. Mains electricity and water (not metered); septic tank; oil-fired central heating. The property is within the Smarden Conservation Area. The septic tank is shared with 1 Forge Cottages and located in its garden; access rights for maintenance; emptying costs shared. The rear of the garden is in Flood Zone 2 (Environment Agency map); the house has not flooded. The seller does not know whether the shared septic tank meets the Environment Agency's 2020 general binding rules. There is restricted head height at the top of the stairs, approximately 1.88m (6'2").
